reviews.text: I finally made it to Mount Emei to witness the spectacular scenery and the famous Sea of Clouds. The man-made structures at the Golden Summit including the Golden, Silver, and Bronze temples are equally breathtaking. Tips and Observations: Chengdu to the Base: A private car from Chengdu to the foot of the mountain takes approximately 2.5 hours. The Scenic Bus: From the base, you must take a scenic sightseeing bus up the mountain. It is a very winding 2-hour ride. Pro-Tip: It is vital to note the return bus schedule. During my visit, the last bus was at 6:00 PM. Do not cut it too close, or you could be stranded on the mountain overnight! The Hike to the Cable Car: Once off the bus, there is an approximately 1.5 km walk to the cable car station. Wildlife Warning: Be careful of the wild monkeys along this path. They are known to snatch plastic bags if they think they contain food. The Summit: The cable car ride to the top takes about 5–10 minutes. From there, you walk further up to reach the grand golden statue of Puxian Bodhisattva and the surrounding temples. Final Verdict: Because this trip involves roughly 9 hours of total travel time from Chengdu, it feels like a once-in-a-lifetime experience. For those who want to see the sunrise or sunset, you can plan to stay at one of the hotels located directly on the mountain to avoid the long day-trip commute. Pack light though as you have to carry your luggages uphill.

To reach the top , first there was the shuttle bus ride then had to hike up the mountain to the cableway station. There was monkeys along the way with some very aggressively looking for food. At the cableway, 100 people were packed into a single ride so you have to be either the first or last on to be able to get a view on the way. After getting off, had to hike again to reach the summit with the giant Buddha and gold, silver and bronze halls. Apart from the summit there is another cableway which is for the Wangnian Temple. From there, it was a leisure trek downhill with alot of hostels overlooking a very peaceful lake.
Fabulous place. Thousands of steps to the summit though. The Golden Buddha is spectacular though well worth the visit. Great food along the way too. Monkeys come close but steal.food be careful. l

Honestly one of the most magical places I've been to in China. I came here on an early winter day, so we were climbing the stairs in a thick mist with all the branches still covered in ice from the nights frost. Once you reach the top and the sun starts piercing through the clouds you'll understand why the temple was build here. I would strongly advice to get the first bus from the tourist center as it gets really busy later on and you'll have the most serene experience. Have fun!
Difficult climb but lots of temples to stay overnight. Expect no heater, veg food, and no English
Speechless! Amazing and awesome! So glad i get the chance to come w my family! If you are buddhism and zodiac dragon or snake do come here at least once in a lifetime 🙂

If you are seeking a mountain/nature experience, seek elsewhere! This is more of a Buddhist cultural experience, to see a massive gold tribute to Buddha made up of elephants, bodisattvas and statues. Thousands of visitors come to pay homage, circling three times in prayer. 90 minutes by shuttle bus from Emei transport station; 20 - 30 minutes up stairs; and 20 minutes (if you are lucky) up to 45 minutes wait in queues for a 100 person crowded 10 minute cable car ride. Or you could walk the 6km 600 m vertical ascent, if the altitude doesn't bother you. Often cloudy and cold at the 3077m top so don't expect views.

Beautiful on a good day, but horrendous visibility on a rainy and wet day. Look up the forecast before you come as it's a two to four hour journey at the very least to get up to the top (including the crowded gondola and ~2,000 step walk uphill).

I visited Emei Mountain a few years ago, and the experience still lingers in my memory like the mountain's ever-present mist. Starting our journey from Chengdu, we hopped on a bullet train, which was fast and comfortable. Once we arrived, we switched to a bus > Cable car that took us up the mountain—a ride that felt like an adventure in itself. I remember we had to pay at several checkpoints along the way, but the excitement of heading toward the summit made it all feel worth it. As we climbed higher, the landscape transformed into a dreamy, surreal world. The mountain was blanketed in thick clouds and mist, giving everything an ethereal, almost otherworldly vibe. While we couldn’t see much of the panoramic views that Emei is famous for, the atmosphere was so peaceful and mystical that it didn’t matter. In fact, the mist made it even more beautiful in its own quiet, magical way. We spent the night at a small inn on the mountain, which added a rustic charm to the whole experience. In the morning, we made our way back to Chengdu, hearts full and cameras foggy. Even without the clear skies, Emei Mountain left a lasting impression—one of serenity, beauty, and a touch of the divine.

Mount Emei Golden Summit, one of the World Heritage Sites for both natural and cultural heritages, is an enhanced combination of lursh forest and monasteries, stunning scenery and profound culture. It's one of the Four Great Buddhist Mountains in China and play an important role in Buddhism. A great place to visit and hiking as a choice for natural lovers.

Takes 1.5 hours from Emei Mountain Station (bullet train) to reach the cable car stop. Then some climbing and walking for 15 minutes from the cable car stop to the cable car queue. There is plentiful of food and drinks along the way to the cable car queue. Depending on the season you are here, the queue can take from 15 mins to a hour. After the cable car ride, expect to walk and climb more stairs to reach the golden peak. Please factor in the travelling time (at least 4 hours round trip. I did it as a day trip from Chengdu. Took the 835am train and reached the bullet train station at 10am. Reached the peak at about 12pm. Departed the peak at 230 and returned to Chengdu at about 7pm. The view is awesome but so the entry ticket price. Note that the initial ticket purchased at the bullet train station does not include the cable car right to the peak. Remember to top up at the ticketing counter before joining the queue!

Literally walking in the clouds in Emei Shan. Quite a number of stairs to climb up to the 4 faced buddha. A 3,099-metre-tall mountain in Sichuan Province, China, and is the highest of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains of China. Be prepared to climb!
The view is great, above the clouds. But, it’s high altitude place. Almost stairs all the way up. So if you have heart condition/high blood pressure, can skip.

A very nice place to visit, and a must go! However, the journey is long and tiring. We took a 1.5 hrs bus up to the mountain, and need to walk 5-10 mins to change to cable car. There are 2 types of cable car, one that carry 6 people (longer waiting time) and the bigger one can carry about 30 paxs at one go. After that, you still need to walk about 15-20 on staircases to reach the top. Very tiring journey, and prepare a whole day there.

2023 December. Once in a lifetime must go place. Not suitable for some as it is quite steep at the last stretch although there are handheld carriages which bring you up with a cost. One day trip. Bring Passport for foreigners. Take the earliest high speed train from Chengdu to Emeishan station 620am+-, economy ticket CNY70+-, 1hr 20min+- duration. Reached the station, go to the official counter and buy entrance ticket, to and fro bus and cable car tickets, approximately CNY400+-. 1st sector, approximately 2hr bus ride, half way through toilet break. 2nd sector, walk approximately 40mins. 3rd sector, cable car approximately 5mins and stroll 10 min to the peak. Lastly enjoy the scenery.

Not cheap to go up here, 90 rmb for shuttle bus 2 ways, 160 rmb for ticket to go to the peak, 120 rmb for cable car 2 ways. Its very cold and iced this time,but if you dont have warm clothes you can hire coat here with 30 rmb only, very convenient and dont need to carry much thing. Scenery is beautiful though toilet is stink and not clean.

One of the most beautiful summits I've been to, Mount Emei [ swipe left for the vid ] and its Golden Summit , It's a mountain in Sichuan Province, China, and is one of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains of China with an elevation of 3099m. The best way to experience it is with a night hike arriving at the top before sunrise as the view of a sun above the clouds is just magical [ but u will have to pray for a clear sky top🙏 ] there is a hotel at the top that u can access with cable car for people who aren't into hiking. On the way back from Mount Emei, u should stop at Leshan for a visit to Leshan big buddha [ 3rd pic ], a 71m statue that took 90 years to crave. Both sites are within a drive from Chengdu

I grew up in a small town not far from Mt. Emei. It is a mountain that my family visited every a couple of years. I have climbed it from bottom to top at least 6 times in different seasons and every time I enjoyed it very much. It is a combination of nature and culture (Buddhism). Recommended to people who come to visit Sichuan/Chengdu. It is a top destination! Summer is the high-season for local people to enjoy the coolness (expensive and crowded). Way less people in the winter and you will see the mountain all covered with snow since the waist of it, marvelous view as well. However, should be careful and suggest to wear a pair of shoes which is suitable for walking on ice. TIPS: Some tempels actually host people for a small amount of fee. The most beautiful temple is Wannian Temple. It was built about 1, 500 years ago. I have stayed there twice and it was about 20-40rmb per person per night in a twin room (very basic room and only public toilet outside, no shower available?). But it was an amazingly unique experience!!
very steep mountain and mid-to-difficult trails. yet, very rewarding scenes. the mountains, temples, villages, monkeys, all mingled naturally.

Do not go if you cannot climb . Very tiring as there are too many stairs There are personal bamboo carriers provided. I paid RMB 580 to go first level n after cable car you need to climb another 30mins to reach the top. Rmb480 fees are chargeable for the 2nd level . Descending, i suggest to walk down .i vomitted as the journey are shaky. The oxygen tank i purchased are of not much use. I felt sleepy due to lack of oxygen. Cable car each cabin takes up too 100person. Everyone are being squeezed together. In btw the hiking there are many stalls selling food n drinks. This place not for elderly
Well manage logistics can handle large crowd. Food and drink available along the way mostly accept only cashless.

I would really recomend you to visit the buddha statue of Mount Emei in Leshan China. Located in the center of Golden Summit, the four sides of the statue are the signs of Mount Emei. The icon was cast in copper-cast gilt and consists of a pedestal and the Ten Prophets. Against the background of the blue sky, the statues give off a shocking glow. Samantabhadra is a symbol of the wish of Mahayana Buddhism. The "Ten Parties" represent the top 10 wishes of Samantabhadra, and it is also a symbol of ten directions in Buddhism. It means that the boundless line of Samantabhadra will be able to complete all the Buddhas of the Ten Trinity III and all sentient beings 🙏🙏🙏

The Golden Summit is absolutely stunning! It was very rewarding especially after 7km of steps and steps and some more steps :) We reached the summit at around 3pm and found out later that this is actually the best time to see the clouds beneath you from the summit. Loved it! A note for other hikers: we did the lower part of Mount Emei on one day and the other day we took the bus and walked the last 7km to the summit. This way you can see the whole mountain without carrying your stuff/sleeping up somewhere. Keep in mind that tickets + bus are expensive. Last but not least: don't forget to bring a jacket - 15 degrees temperature difference between bottom and top

I came to 峨眉山 in January 2019 winter. It was super cold. Took a 2 day 1 night tour from the city. Mount Emei is absolutely stunning but I did not get to see any sunshine despite being there at 5am in the morning due to the dense fog. You might even encounter some wild monkeys along the way down the hill.
Great views. Too crowded during holidays. Can make it as real adventurous hike of 2-3 days or you can take vehicles halfway through the mountains and finish it in one day too.

Early Jan 2024 How does this place get 4.6 stars rating ? Personally, I don’t think this place is worth the time and money. 1) We visited Mount Emei for its thousand years old history. But the four faces golden Buddha at the top was built in 2006. And most temples, statues and structures at the top are all relatively new. We may have missed something but we didn’t see anything that resembles thousands years old. 2) A temple is not supposed to collect entrance fee. This place does. 160 yuan per adult ticket. Plus you have to pay for bus tickets and most likely pay for the optional cable car 🚠 which are not cheap. They pack 100 persons into one cable car and people would un-politely race and push for good spots in the packed cable car. And the view going up is not as impressive Tianmen Mountain 3) it collects high entrance fee but doesn’t maintain the bathrooms clean and the path clean. You will enter dirty bathrooms and see many trashes along the climb 4) while many tour guides don’t use loud speakers here but many shops do. The speakers noise are annoying. Isn’t mountain temple and its paths are supposed to be peaceful and quiet? 5) along the way, vendors all sell similar products. These stalls are most likely owned by the same companies. There is no uniqueness to the shops 6) Visiting Mount Emei feel like visiting a tourist attraction instead a holy ancient temples. It is too commercialized for profit. I do not think this place is worth the money if not the time also. I doubt how many are remained from the thousand years old temple. The name Emei temple are used to attract tourist to the modern built temples and statues. Would not recommend this place for the price and time one needs to spend to get up there. Not worth the money and effort.

Holy place I visited here in Feb 2013. There still remained snow. Before climbing, I put non-slipper-item on my shoes. That was a little tough walking. But when I arrived at the top there, my body was totally refreshed by the big buddha. That was one of my unforgettable memories in my life. Thank, God. Hope so many people visit here and experience their own emancipation.
Emei Moutain is very nice place to visit, you can see the snow in the winter time and lots of funny monkeys, but you need be carefull about them :)
Mount Emei is a sacred mountain in China with a beautiful monastery at the top. We used the cable car to get up but walked down.

One of the most beautiful views I have ever seen. Word of advice, if you can, get a hotel room on the mountain. It will give you more time to explore and WAY less time travelling. The mountain range and scenic ares are much bigger than some would think. Definitely a bucket list place to go

A good and highland place to visit near ChengDu. First you have to reach Emei city, famous for tea production and for local foods. The bus service is available from here to cable car station. It takes three hour upland drive, then you can get cable car to temple. Bus+cable car+visit ticket is expensive ¥250. If you reach there little late then you may feel difficulty to return on time. It will be better for you take high speed rail from ChengDu and return from Emei city. Good place to visit.

Zero experience. Even though the forecast claimed that it was going to be a mildly cloudy morning with 5h of sunshine, there was only thick fog. You couldn't see further than 20m on the summit. No views, no monkeys, only crowds and stalls. Weathered facilities. Unimpressive cable car ride in the fog obviously. Total ripoff. The only thing worth the money was the bus ride.

In 2015 did the two day hike, stone stairs all the way up! We encountered few people and a small temple and the infamous monkeys of Emei Shan! Didn't have conditions for the "sea of clouds" but totally worth it! Thanks to local friends who arranged the overnight stay and wonderful hosts!

I visited this mountain during the August of 2018. The views at the top are incredible, and you'll see lots of monkeys along the way too! We took a bus to the last bus top (leidongping) and hiked about 8km to the Golden Summit (jinding). You can also take a cable car instead, but we decided to go for a challenge. At the Golden Summit, there were great views of the peak soaring high above the clouds. When we arrived at the peak to watch the sunrise, we were amazed to see a sea of clouds and fog stretching far out into the horizon, with the sun rising in the distance. It was truly beautiful. There is also huge temperature difference. When we went (in the middle of summer), the bottom was around 30 C and the top was around 10 C (getting colder at night). So be prepared with a sweater and maybe a jacket. I also found the higher altitude made the hike significantly harder, but it wasn't too bad. The great views at the top was truly worth it!

Was visiting Chengdu & Leshan China in May-June 2017, Made it a day trip and I wish I could have stayed longer. It would have been quite the experience hiking up the mountain from the other reviews I was reading. If I were to do it again, I would hike and stay where I could. Beautiful views, wild monkeys who steal food/drinks, & a workout. Golden summit is a cultural place and I would definitely recommend to anyone who enjoys an adventure. I ended up taking a tour bus up & cable cars. Good views, but not the experience hiking would have been. Cloudy day atop the mountain, wished it was clear.

Getting to the top of the mountain is easy since you will take a cable car and then climb a short way. But at the top it is difficult to see much because there is often a fog. You will almost never see the buddhist tower (which has been permanently closed to tourism) that is about 1 km away at the edge of the cliff. At the top, there is golden buddha which you can go in and offer prayers as well as a few surrounding temples.

We visited in December, it was very cold and snowing our entire visit. It was an amazing experience even though the snow restricted the view from the top and of the golden summit. It was still worth the hike, when visiting in winter be sure to take snow shoes and rain gear

The road to reach the Golden Summit is another important part of experience to be had. Make sure you don't eat too much before hand. Bring your water and watch the slippery road during winter. Plus, monkeys also another thing to look out for on the way up.

Mount Emei is located on the southwestern edge of the Sichuan Basin. It has become a treasure for mankind with its beautiful and secluded natural scenery, rich biological resources and profound historical and cultural heritage. As one of the four famous Buddhist mountains in China, it has accumulated a large number of relics such as temples, calligraphy, paintings and inscriptions. Located at the foot of Mount Emei, the Leshan Giant Buddha is a statue of Maitreya sitting on the mountain. It faces the confluence of the Minjiang, Dadu and Qingyi rivers. The statue is more than 70m tall and has a history of more than 1,000 years. In 1996, the Mount Emei-Leshan Giant Buddha Scenic Spot was approved by Unesco as a World Cultural and Natural Heritage site.
Took the bus, waived the cable car and walked the last couple of hours. Beautiful up there. Worth another day hiking some of the trails. Theres a lot to see. Hotels everywhere.

There's a lot of Legends surrounding this mountain it also takes place around Legend of the White Snake and is where Lady Bai is supposed to live and her sister Xiao Qing. Legend has it a White snake fell in love with a mortal man Xu Xian which heavenly laws for some reason forbid immortals to fall in love with mortals. The snake was then wrongfully sealed by Monk Fahai underneath Hangzhou's Leifeng Pagoda eventually it seems the building corroded over time and the White Snake was freed. Another Legend states Xiao Qing the blue snake sister of Bai Suzhen or Lady Bai destroyed the Pagoda and freed her sister. Really interesting story the best replay is to watch Sorcerer and the White Snake and to watch White Snake on VUDU and Green Snake on Netflix sets a good combination for english people to watch. One of these days I am going to visit this Mountain because of Legend of the White Snake I wish to detour Leifeng Pagoda as well not the original which is a bummer but worth looking into!
Spectacular scenic tour. Good fitness is required, but the experience is priceless. Definitely one tick off my bucket list.
Is a must place to visit! fresh air nice view! But paying 120RMB to take the cable car and still need to climb stairs up and fown bout 5KM 😑

Mt emei earliest bus from Chengdu RMB 50. Check into hot spring hotel, leave baggage and proceed to Mt Leshan Buddha by bus 601. RMB 5. Come back to hotel and soak in the hot spring. RMB 550 with bf and free usage of hot pool. Tomorrow go up Mt emei to enjoy the fantastic view.
What a spectacular place to enjoy the mountains. Try to choose a time with less tourists to really enjoy the old world charm and serenity.
Life is like a book, when you open a new page, a new word emerges like new feelings, new moments or new passage.,,,,,nice place
This is One Of One of the most beautiful places in lashan in Sichuan province China and Took 90 years to build
I went there as a school trip leader. It was incredible. Worth every painful step!! 😃
stupid mountain caretakers, where the donkeys are worked hard until they are completely exhausted! karma is waiting for you!
Tourist place...here everyone look for a way to catch your money...I stayed four years ago, and now i'm really disappointed how everything changed.

Golden Summit at an altitude of 3000m, like a celestial paradise, the golden Buddha statue, 48m high and weighing 660 tons, faces in ten directions, along with the Golden Temple, Silver Temple, and Bronze Temple. This creates a magnificent religious architectural complex.
一個充滿情懷的景點 從前在金庸小說裡聽過 來到現場 雪地裡、登山客、野猴群 遠眺普賢菩薩 內心衝擊 感動、震撼百感交集 難怪 峨眉金頂享譽盛名 來一次,真的不枉此行

ถึงแม้ว่าการเดินทางจะขึ้นมาด้วยความยากลำบาก แต่พอขึ้นมามาถึงแล้วความเหนื่อยทั้งหมดได้หายไป อยู่ดีๆก็มีความรู้สึกสบายใจขึ้น ได้อย่างบอกไม่ถูกเลย ทั้งทั้งที่ไม่ได้มีเรื่องทุกข์ใจอะไร ￼ แต่มีความรู้สึกว่า ทุกอย่างมันโล่งไปหมดเลย 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻 ไม่ผิดหวังที่ขึ้นมาถึงยอดเขา มันสวยมากจริงๆค่ะ ￼
峨眉山是佛教四大名山之一 普賢菩薩的道場 上峨眉山最高金頂 這次我們是走最輕鬆的路線 從報國寺做2小時接駁車至 雷洞坪的 先走40分鐘階梯上接引殿 再坐纜車輕鬆至金頂

Hah??? Sampai puncak harus melewati 900an tangga!! Itupun ada yang harus naik cable car....jadi urutannya naik tangga, cabke car, naik tangga lagi....baru sampai puncak. Begitu juga pulangnya. Jujur....capekkk!! Dari 20 orang hanya 7 yg sampai puncak. Yang lain nunggu di tengah2 setelah cable car ada beberapa tempat peristirahatan dan warung2...sehingga bisa sambil makan minum untuk menunggu yg pada naik turun kembali.
这几天天气太好了 勇闯峨眉山！ 已经来过三四次了 大晴天的峨眉山还第一次来 登山远眺 居然还能看到瓦屋山 还有蜀山之王贡嘎山！！！ 哦买嘎 峨眉山的猴子哥也是见识了 一个二个肥噔噔的 肆无忌惮抢游客 猴子多的荡一股尿骚味 峨眉山又陡又险 原来来云雾多还看不咋出来 巴适克特博
Bello ma la salita con il bus dura 1:30. Consiglio vivamente di scendere a piedi. Foresta magica
Núi cao, đường đi quanh co,khúc khuỷu. Đi bộ nhiều, có dịch vụ khiêng cáng cho người già, yếu. Là địa điểm nổi tiếng nên đáng để đi một lần.

峨眉山真的是一个让我难忘的地方！这里不仅风景美得让人窒息，还有浓厚的文化底蕴。从山脚到山顶的每一段路程都充满了惊喜，尤其是早晨看到的云海，真的是如梦似幻。一路上还能遇到很多可爱的猴子，不过要小心它们“抢”东西哦！爬山虽然有点累，但一路的风景完全值得。金顶的视野特别开阔，可以俯瞰整个峨眉山的景色，特别壮观。如果不想走路，也可以选择坐索道上去，方便又快捷。无论你是喜欢户外运动的，还是想要寻找一处心灵的净土，峨眉山绝对不会让你失望。建议大家带上一些干粮和水，这样更能享受整个旅程。总之，峨眉山绝对是一个来了就不想走的地方，五星推荐，强烈建议大家来体验一下这座中国的名山！

峨眉山，也稱峨嵋山，金庸小說常見到的武俠聖地.位於中國四川省峨眉山市境內，最高峰萬佛頂(3,099米)，佛教聖地華藏寺所在地金頂（3,077米）為峨眉山旅遊的最高點。地勢陡峭，風景秀麗，有「峨眉天下秀」之美稱。氣候多樣化，植被異常豐富，共有3,000多種植物。山路沿途有較多猴群，常成群結隊向遊人討食掠食，遊客儘量避免手提食物或塑膠袋。峨眉山是中國四大佛教名山之一，有寺廟約26座，重要的有八大寺廟，佛事頻繁。據傳為佛教中普賢菩薩的道場。於1996年12月6日，峨眉山—樂山大佛作為一項文化與自然雙重遺產被聯合國教科文組織列入世界遺產名錄。
佛教四大名山。天空不作美。山在雲霧裊裊中。假日人潮眾多，如果在大日子來參訪要有心理準備。上山下山都必須花很多的時間。聽說一年365天有300天都是在雲霧當中，所以今天來看不見任何的美景也屬於正常。

Một nơi rất đáng để tham quan, thời tiết tháng tư rất đẹp, ít sương mù, nắng đẹp, tuy lạnh và có Tuyết nên càng tô điểm cho núi và các ngôi chùa tren núi cũng như phong cảnh càng thêm đẹp, ko thể tả bằng lời , rất đẹp . Mong sẽ có cơ hội quay lại

Parti en bus à 8h30 de la station de bus à Emeishan puis en télécabine pour rejoindre le sommet. Redescendu par la même voie (grand téléphérique au retour). Retour à 17h. On a pas mal traîné et visité. Le trajet entre le parking et les télécabine puis entre les télécabines et le sommet nécessite un petit effort. Il faut monter des escaliers plusieurs minutes. Mais l'effort est raisonnable si on s'arrêt régulièrement (nous avions une dame de 75 ans avec nous qui a fait l'aller retour). Il y a des marchands tout le long de la route. Vous ne mourrez ni de faim ni de soif :) Le spectacle en haut est magnifique. Nous avons eu beau temps et avons pu admirer la mer de nuage. Attention aux singes ! Ne laissez rien traîner ou dépasser de votre sac !

普陀山，為觀世音菩薩道場，水。 五臺山，為文殊菩薩道場，風。 峨嵋山，為普賢菩薩道場，火。 九華山，為地藏菩薩道場，地。 佛經稱地藏、觀音、普賢、文殊諸佛道場，曰地、水、火、風，為四大結聚。九華，地也；普陀，水也；峨眉，火也；五臺，風也。
楽山大仏と共にとして世界遺産（複合遺産=文化遺産+自然遺産）に認定されている。標高3,000m級の山だが、いや、まぁ、中国という国のスケールのでかさに圧倒される。

霧深い四川の地の美しい自然が魅力です。ここは楽山大仏と同じく、文化と自然の両面からの遺産価値が評価された世界でもまだ数少ない複合遺産です。今では観光地としての開発が進んでいますが、現地でも聖地として考えられているため、それでも手付かずの豊かな自然が多く残り、さまざまな種類の動植物を見る事ができます。かなり歩くので、水や食料を買い込み、動きやすい服と靴とで観光に臨みましょう。また雨も多いと聞いたので、雨具もあると安心です。

Site exceptionnel !! Je suis parti tout seul et j'ai rencontré 2 français au Teddy Bear Hostel donc nous avons tout fait ensemble. Vous pouvez y laisser vos affaires gratuitement pour monter léger. L'ascension se fait en minimun 1.5 jours (50km), et encore le rythme du premier fut difficile. Nous avons mis 8h en traînant légèrement pour attendre le monastère Elephant Batling Pool (lit avec couverture chauffante, pas besoin de réserver c'est immense) et y passer la nuit. Le lendemain nous avons mis 4h pour atteindre le sommet. Autant dire que la meilleure partie est avant le somment car finalement peu de personne font cette ascension assez sportive. En haut il y a les bus qui arrivent donc c'est bondé, mais la vision du sommet est exceptionnelle après ce rude périple. Bâton obligatoire pour les singes, bâton vertical tapper au sol pour les faire fuir. Il y avait un peu de neige au sommet mi-octobre donc prévoir en fonction de la saison. Nous sommes redescendu en téléphérique pour le fun et bus car très fatigué, mais la descente est possible à pied, il vaut dans ce cas mieux une nuit supplémentaire dans la descente dans un monastère pour prendre son temps. Expérience à faire absolument.

峨眉山，亦作峨嵋山[1]，位于中国四川省峨眉山市境内，景区面积154平方公里，最高峰万佛顶海拔3099米[2]，于2007年以前可乘观光索道到达，官方解釋因生态问题停止对外开放，亦有稱係投資方糾紛關停，佛教圣地华藏寺所在地金顶（3077米）成为了峨眉山旅游的最高点。地势陡峭，风景秀丽，有“峨眉天下秀”之美誉。气候多样化，植被丰富，共有3000多种植物，其中包括世界上稀有的树种。山路沿途有较多猴群，常结队向游人讨食，胜为峨眉一大特色。它是中国四大佛教名山之一，有寺庙约26座，重要的有八大寺庙，佛事频繁。据传为佛教中普贤菩萨的道场。1996年12月6日，峨眉山—乐山大佛作为一项文化与自然双重遗产被联合国教科文组织列入世界遗产名录。 Mount Emei, also known as Lushan, is located in Emeishan City, Sichuan Province, China. The scenic area is 154 square kilometers. The highest peak Wanfoding is 3,99 meters above sea level. It can be reached by sightseeing cableway before 2007. The official explanation is that it will stop opening to the public due to ecological problems. There was a dispute over the investment of the investor, and the Golden Summit (3,077 meters) where the Buddhist holy place of Huazang Temple was located became the highest point of tourism in Mount Emei. The terrain is steep and the scenery is beautiful. It has the reputation of “Emei World Show”. The climate is diverse and the vegetation is rich, with more than 3,000 species of plants, including rare species in the world. There are more monkeys along the mountain roads, often teaming up for tourists to eat, winning a big feature of Emei. It is one of the four famous Buddhist mountains in China. There are about 26 temples, and there are eight major temples. The Buddha is frequent. It is said to be the dojo of Buddhism in Buddhism. On December 6, 1996, the Emeishan-Leshan Giant Buddha was listed as a World Heritage by UNESCO as a double heritage of culture and nature.

峨眉山，亦作峨嵋山，位于中国四川省峨眉山市境内，景区面积154平方公里，最高峰万佛顶海拔3099米，于2007年以前可乘观光索道到达，后因生态问题停止对外开放，佛教圣地华藏寺所在地金顶（3077米）成为了峨眉山旅游的最高点。地势陡峭，风景秀丽，有“峨眉天下秀”之美誉。气候多样化，植被丰富，共有3000多种植物，其中包括世界上稀有的树种。山路沿途有较多猴群，常结队向游人讨食，胜为峨眉一大特色。它是中国四大佛教名山之一，有寺庙约26座，重要的有八大寺庙，佛事频繁。据传为佛教中普贤菩萨的道场。1996年12月6日，峨眉山—乐山大佛作为一项文化与自然双重遗产被联合国教科文组织列入世界遗产名录。 金顶为峨眉山主峰，海拔3077米，是峨眉游山的终点，名胜云集。华藏寺高耸于岩顶，建于唐朝，屋顶为锡瓦所盖，元代时又被称为“银顶”。寺侧有卧云庵，内有饭堂和客房可供游客食宿。在金顶可观看峨眉四大奇观——日出、云海、佛光、圣灯。金顶与千佛顶、万佛顶相邻，万佛顶上亦有建筑，且有观光索道连接金顶与接引殿。 报国寺位于峨眉山麓，是步入峨眉的门户，举行各种佛事活动的中心。该寺创建于明万历年间，曾名“会宗堂”，寺内供奉着佛教始祖释迦牟尼的大弟子普贤菩萨、道教创始人的化身广成子、春秋名士陆通，取儒、道、释三教会宗合祀之意。清康熙帝取佛门“报国主恩”之意，改名报国寺。全寺占地近4万平方米，山门、弥勒殿、大雄殿、七佛殿、普贤殿、藏经楼等，自前至后沿中轴线逐渐升高。周围有花影亭、七香轩、吟翠楼、待月山房等雅致建筑。

四川唯一一处联合国自然、文化，双料遗产。但是，几个著名的景点，已经被过度消费过于商业化了。峨眉山真正的风景，是在，从“天下名山”牌坊处一路徒步到金顶的沿途。沿着石板路慢慢走，一路十数个没什么商业气息的寺院和自然风景融为一体，可以慢慢体会宗教与自然的结合。缺点，累，节假日看人头。

Núi Nga Mi – là một trong Tứ Đại Danh Sơn của Phật Giáo Trung Hoa, là đạo trường của Phổ Hiền Bồ Tát và cũng là ngọn núi linh thiêng đối với người Trung Quốc. Bạn có thể tham quan : - Báo Quốc Tự – là ngôi chùa nổi tiếng nhất núi Nga Mi, được xây dựng từ cuối thế kỷ 16. - Kim Đỉnh – nơi cao nhất của núi Nga Mi với độ cao hơn 3.000m, cảnh vật hai bên sườn núi như bồng lai tiên cảnh, mờ mờ ảo ảo, thoắt ẩn thoắt hiện - Chùa Vàng – ngôi chùa được sơn lớp vàng óng ánh, là nơi thờ Phổ Hiền Bồ Tát linh thiêng với bảng treo hai chữ Kim Đỉnh bằng vàng nguyên khối. - Tượng Phổ Hiền Bồ Tát – được đúc bằng đồng, bên ngoài mạ hơn 20kg vàng, cao khoảng 48m và là tượng Phật vàng cao nhất thế giới. - Chùa Bạc – khối kiến trúc được sơn một lớp bạc hết sức trang trọng và là nơi thỉnh các bảo pháp Phật giáo. - Chùa Đồng – sở hữu điện thờ lớn nhất và lâu đời nhất tại Kim Đỉnh, điện có kết cấu bằng đồng.

Nga Mi sơn ([ɤ̌.měi]; tiếng Trung: 峨眉山; bính âm: Éméi shān) hay núi Nga Mi còn được gọi là Đại Quang Minh sơn là một ngọn núi nằm ở tỉnh Tứ Xuyên, Trung Quốc, trên khu vực rìa phía tây của lòng chảo Tứ Xuyên theo hướng cao nguyên Thanh-Tạng. Nó cao 3.099 mét (10.167 ft) và là Tứ đại Phật giáo danh sơn, một trong bốn ngọn núi thiêng của Trung Quốc. Những ngọn núi phía tây của Nga Mi được gọi là Đại Tương Lĩnh. Đây là một vùng rộng lớn được hình thành bởi những trận phun trào núi lửa trong kỷ Permi. Về mặt hành chính, Nga Mi sơn nằm gần như hoàn toàn trong thành phố cấp huyện Nga Mi Sơn và một phần nhỏ thuộc Lạc Sơn. Nó cùng với Lạc Sơn Đại Phật được UNESCO công nhận là Di sản thế giới từ năm 1996.
